title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the last page of the 1986 'Analysis situs (quatrième mouture)' notes. Grothendieck is reworking the elementary combinatorics of 'figures' on a totally ordered set L, in the spirit of the 'tame topology' programme announced in the Esquisse (1984). The setting, inferred from this page and the previous one, is as follows.

- A figure Φ is a finite union of 'cells': points of L and open 'intertypic' intervals between consecutive points.
- δΦ ⊂ L is a finite 'flag' (an element of Drap^L(L)). It is the set of points used to present Φ, namely the points of Φ_0 and the endpoints of the intervals of Φ_1. It is not the topological boundary, since it may contain 'redundant' points. The previous page splits Δ = Δ_is ⊔ Δ_red ⊔ Δ_loc ⊔ ∂Ψ accordingly.
- For a finite Δ, Φ_Δ is the 'standard' cell decomposition. Its points (Φ_Δ)_0 = Δ, and its open intervals (Φ_Δ)_1 are those between consecutive elements of Δ.

At the end of p.117 Grothendieck proposes a simpler presentation. A préfigure is the datum of Δ ∈ Drap(L), a subset Φ_1 ⊂ (Φ_Δ)_1 and a subset Φ_0 ⊂ Δ. This page completes that remark.

Step 1. The union Φ_0 ∪ Φ_1 is a figure, but in general one only has δ(Φ_0 ∪ Φ_1) ⊂ Δ. The inclusion can be strict, e.g. Φ_0 = Φ_1 = ∅.

Step 2. One therefore imposes a condition, apparently labelled 'Pur(D_Δ)'. For every s ∈ Δ \ Φ_0 there is an X ∈ Φ_1 with s ⊲ X, i.e. s is an endpoint (face) of X. Equivalently Δ = Φ_0 ∪ ⋃_{X∈Φ_1} ∂X. This says exactly that every point of Δ is genuinely used by the presentation.

Step 3. A marginal note treats the degenerate case. If Δ = ∅ then Φ_Δ = ∅, Φ = ∅ and the condition is trivial.

Step 4. He defines the complementary préfigure Φ'^* with the same Δ:
- Φ'^*_0 = (Φ_Δ)_0 \ Φ_0 = Δ \ Φ_0;
- Φ'^*_1 = (Φ_Δ)_1 \ Φ_1.

Step 5. With Δ ≠ ∅, put a = or(Δ) (its least element) and b = ex(Δ) (its greatest element). Put M_{<a} = {X ∈ M | X < a} and M_{>b} = {X ∈ M | X > b}. Here M appears to be the underlying set or 'model' whose points are 'shadowed' by cells of L, via Omb°.

Step 6. By hypothesis, M_{<a} = ∅ iff a is the least element of L, and M_{>b} = ∅ iff b is the greatest element of L. One then gets the disjoint union
Compr°(Φ) = Omb°(Φ'^*) ∪ M_{<a} ∪ M_{>b},
where Omb°(Φ'^*) is by definition ⋃_{X∈Φ'^*} Omb°(X), itself a disjoint union.

In words, the open shadow of the complement of a figure is the union of three disjoint pieces: the shadows of the complementary cells inside [a,b], and the two unbounded end-pieces below a and above b.

The problem this serves is to give a clean combinatorial description of figures and of their complements. That is the basis for a complement/duality operation Φ ↦ Φ'^* in a one-dimensional tame-topology formalism.
errors: The formula for Compr° is written with Φ'^* carrying a struck or ambiguous subscript ('Φ'^*_1' in the transcription). The next line defines Omb°(Φ'^*) over all cells of Φ'^*, points and intervals. So the intended statement is most likely Compr°(Φ) = Omb°(Φ'^*) ∪ M_{<a} ∪ M_{>b}, with the points Δ \ Φ_0 included. If only Φ'^*_1 were meant, the points of Δ \ Φ_0 would be missing from the complement.

a and b are undefined for Δ = ∅. Grothendieck struck out his 'si Δ ≠ ∅' qualifier and moved the degenerate case to the margin. In that case Compr°(Φ) should simply be all of M. This is a minor gap, not an error.
The text breaks off here (last page of the dossier), so the 'on trouve aussitôt' claim is not verified on the page. It is elementary, though.

ideas.what: Presentation of a (pre)figure on a total order by a finite set Δ of vertices, a subset of vertices and a subset of open intervals of the induced decomposition, with a 'purity' condition Δ = Φ_0 ∪ ⋃ ∂X ensuring Δ is exactly the set used.
ideas.modern_name: one-dimensional cell decomposition / finite subcomplex of a 1-dim stratification (o-minimal cell decomposition in dimension 1)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme of 'topologie modérée' appears, in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). These detailed notes are unpublished.

ideas.what: Complementary préfigure Φ'^* on the same Δ (complementary vertices and complementary intervals), giving a description of the complement's shadow, up to the two unbounded rays.
ideas.modern_name: complement of a subcomplex in a cell decomposition / Boolean algebra of definable subsets of a line

ideas.what: 'Ombre' Omb°(X): the realization in a model/point-set M of a cell of the order L (L apparently an order of 'types' and intertypic intervals), with M_{<a} empty iff a is minimal in L.
ideas.modern_name: realization of cuts/types in an ordered structure; type space of an o-minimal line

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 analysis situs works with an order L of 'types' and 'intertypic intervals' and shadows in a set M. This is contemporaneous with, and apparently independent of, the o-minimal theory of types/cuts on a definable line. It suggests that his tame-topology formalism was being built over a type-space-like object rather than a point set. The link with o-minimal type spaces is not made in the literature on Grothendieck's tame topology.
missed.quote: Par hyp., M_{<a} est ∅ ssi a est un plus petit élément de L, et M_{>b} est vide ssi b est un plus grand élément de L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild historical interest for comparing Grothendieck's unpublished tame topology with o-minimality. Mathematically this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping for one-dimensional cell decompositions and complements on an ordered set. It is historically part of the unpublished tame-topology notes, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: The figure is denoted Φ (as on p.117), not 𝔏; read Φ_0, Φ_1, Φ_Δ, Φ'^* throughout.
The opening 'Ex[?]' is probably 'NB' or an abbreviation introducing a remark continuing p.117. It is not obviously 'Exemple'.
The condition label reads roughly 'Pur(D_Δ)' or 'Pur(Φ_Δ)'. The relation is s ⊲ X ('s is a face/endpoint of X'), confirmed by the equivalent form Δ = Φ_0 ∪ ⋃ ∂X.
Margin: 'Si Δ=∅, Φ_Δ=∅, Φ=∅ et condition triviale; si Δ≠∅ ...'.
In the Compr° formula the subscript on Φ'^* appears struck; the intended term is most likely Omb°(Φ'^*), consistent with the following definition line.
The final marginal words read 'réunion disjointe'.
